name: Equatorial Guinea
summary_text: Equatorial Guinea is dangerous for trans visitors. The 2022 penal code does not explicitly criminalise same-sex conduct — but a 2024 Synergía report documents twelve women imprisoned between January and August 2024 in police raids led by the Armed Forces and State Security, with detention-for-bribes and indefinite imprisonment; a Draft Law “Regulating Prostitution and the Rights of Homosexuals” (2020, status unclear) would formally criminalise. Africa's longest-ruling dictatorship; no recourse.

sources.claim_summary: Synergia report on lesbophobia, human rights and police raids in Equatorial Guinea: documents police and military interventions in spaces of assembly, expression and residence of lesbian women; in Bata, police detain known lesbians collectively ('lesbians are members of a sect'), including collective punishment when one lesbian is sought.

sources.title: Equatorial Guinea | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): the 2022 penal code does not explicitly criminalise same-sex intimacy or gender diversity, but a Draft Law Regulating Prostitution and the Rights of Homosexuals (2020, status unclear) would effectively criminalise LGBTIQ people; authorities still apply the obsolete 1954 Law on Vagrants and Criminals, which normalises conversion practices and classifies homosexuality as illness; three legal instruments institutionalise discrimination (Military Justice Code, ministerial order on 'immoral' activities, provincial regulation).

sources.title: Equatorial Guinea - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2021 Human Rights Report for Equatorial Guinea: official assessment - same-sex conduct not specifically criminalised but LGBT persons face societal stigma; no anti-discrimination protections; general repression context.

sources.title: Responses to Information Requests - Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada
sources.claim_summary: Canada IRB Response to Information Request on Equatorial Guinea: country-of-origin research citing publicly available information on conditions relevant to refugee claims.

UPR stakeholder submission (Small Media, EG Justice, IPI, Digital Rights in Equatorial Guinea) for Equatorial Guinea's fourth review: focuses on freedom of expression, digital rights and journalist safety - the repressive environment that also constrains LGBT advocacy.

sources.title: The Invisibilities of Equatoguinean Queer Motherhood Revealed in Trifonia Melibea Obono’s Yo no quería ser madre (2019) | Published in Hispanic Studies Review
sources.claim_summary: Hispanic Studies Review (Oct 2025): academic article on Equatoguinean queer motherhood in Trifonia Melibea Obono's novel 'Yo no quería ser madre' (2019) - compulsory heterosexuality and queer invisibility in Equatorial Guinea.
